hook: The dressing gown fits her exactly.
excerpt: On the kitchen wall, a smaller frame. Claire on the terrace with a mug in her right hand, squinting into low sun, in a navy dressing gown with white piping.

excerpt.text: Mine. Or not mine – the same kind.
So he’d bought me one to match. That was either very thoughtful or very strange, and I’d been in enough strange houses to know those weren’t opposites.

excerpt: And two cardboard tags, still joined by a loop of nylon thread, where someone had snipped them off with scissors.

excerpt.text: Coastline & Co. Then, in smaller letters: Terry robe. Navy/white. L – Tall. £68.
Tall. Claire came up to his shoulder. Claire’s robe nearly touched the ground.
Somebody had looked at a woman they’d never met – at a photograph of her, three photographs, a profile on a website – and thought about her arms, and her height, and ordered accordingly.

excerpt: ‘Morning, Claire! Feeling better, love? Daniel said you’d been poorly.’

excerpt.text: The lie is always a little nearer than the truth, and it costs less to pick up.

caption:
The dressing gown fits her exactly. That should have been the first warning.

Ava is house-sitting for an architect whose wife is away. Every morning the neighbour waves from her garden and calls her Claire.

Then she finds the tag in the bin.
